name: Influence
line: Volunteering and a fellowship, nationwide. Ten thousand volunteers a year, and over 300 youth groups.
deck: Ten fellows a year, each one running at a problem in their own neighbourhood. Climate, air, environment, waste. Pick one, then build something.

figures.label: Youth groups in the CYON network

aims.h: Let the fellow choose the problem
aims.p: We do not hand out briefs. The person who spends the year on it has to be the person who picked it, because nobody sustains somebody else's outrage for twelve months.
A fellowship aims at an object in a street rather than a document in a folder. If a year produces a presentation, it has produced nothing.

aims.h: Be a switchboard, not a department
aims.p: The volunteering half works when we are the smallest part of it: somebody with free afternoons, somebody who is short of people, and one introduction.

aims.h: Leave the groups their own names
aims.p: The network is trying to make three hundred groups useful to each other. Not one of them is meant to end up with our logo on it.

how.p: The point of a fellowship year is a thing that exists at the end of it — something built in a neighbourhood, small enough for one person to run and specific enough to argue about.

activities.name: The fellowship
activities.p: Ten a year, and each fellow takes a community project rather than a desk. The brief is a real problem in a real place: climate, air, environment, waste. Four words that cover most of what is going wrong outside your window.
activities.cap: No photograph of a fellow's project is in our hands. Ten a year, and this page can show you none of them.

activities.name: The volunteering switchboard
activities.p: Ten thousand volunteers a year, drawn out of fifty colleges and placed with seventy-five partner organisations. It works like a switchboard: young people on one side, organisations that need hands on the other.

frame.alt: Young volunteers gathered at a planting site

activities.name: CYON
activities.p: A network of over three hundred youth groups. Not our groups — theirs, connected to each other.

frame.alt: Young people clearing weed from a shallow riverbank

activities.cap: Young volunteers of ours at work. Not a CYON group; none of the three hundred is photographed here.

who.h: Young people who want a year, not a workshop
who.p: The fellowship is for somebody prepared to spend a year on one problem in their own neighbourhood. Ten of them a year.
The volunteering programme draws out of fifty colleges. It works for somebody with a term of free afternoons and no idea where to spend them.

who.h: Organisations that are short of hands
who.p: Seventy-five partner organisations take the volunteers. This is as much for them as for the volunteer, and they are the half that is easiest to forget.
Over three hundred of them in the CYON network. They arrived with their own name and their own street; what they get here is each other.

done.h: Ten a year, on four problems
done.p: Ten fellowships every year, each on a community project in climate, air, environment or waste.
Ten thousand volunteers a year, fifty colleges, two hundred placements, seventy-five partner organisations, and a network of over three hundred youth groups.

holes.what: There may be films and case studies of the fellows' projects. We have not put our hands on them, so this page counts fellowships instead of showing one.
holes.unlocks: The films and the case studies. Ten fellows a year and not one of their projects named here is the gap on this page.

holes.what: The volunteering figures are dated to the year the programme started. We cannot say which of them is still true.
holes.unlocks: A current year on any one of the five.

holes.what: How long a fellowship runs is not stated here, because we have not been told.
holes.unlocks: One number: the length of the year.

holes.what: Fifty colleges and seventy-five partner organisations sit behind the volunteering half, and this page names none of them.
holes.unlocks: Five names with permission. It would turn two counts into a list of collaborators, which is what they are.

statement.under: We introduce them to each other and then get out of the way.
